does: Stirs anchovy fillets into warm oil over low heat and presses them with a spoon until they fall apart and vanish into it. They leave a deep savoury taste rather than a fishy one.

intro.what: Anchovy fillets are pressed into warm oil until they dissolve.
intro.why: Melted anchovy gives a sauce depth and salt without any visible fish, a base used across southern Italian cooking.

how: Warm the oil over low heat, with any garlic already in it.
Add the drained fillets and press them against the pan with a wooden spoon.
Keep stirring until no pieces are left and the oil is cloudy, then go on with the sauce.

cues.text: No pieces of fillet are left; the oil looks cloudy and slightly brown.

mistakes.mistake: Frying the fillets in very hot oil, so that they crisp and taste harsh.
mistakes.fix: Keep the heat low and press them so that they melt.

mistakes.mistake: Adding salt before the anchovy has gone in.
mistakes.fix: Taste the finished sauce first: anchovy brings plenty of salt.

quiz.question: What do melted anchovies give a sauce?
choices: A deep savoury taste with no visible fish.
quiz.because: Once dissolved they disappear into the oil and add depth and salt.

quiz.question: How do you help the fillets melt?
choices: Press them with a spoon in warm oil.
quiz.because: Gentle heat and pressure break them down into the oil.

quiz.question: How do you know they have melted?
choices: The fillets are crisp and brown.
The oil is clear and the fillets are whole.
No pieces remain and the oil is cloudy.
quiz.because: Fully melted anchovy leaves no pieces behind.

quiz.question: The sauce came out too salty. What would you change next time?
choices: Taste after the anchovies have melted before adding any salt.
quiz.because: Anchovies are salty, so salt is judged only after they are in.

comes_after.why: The anchovies usually go into oil already flavoured with garlic.

variant_of.differs: Heat alone does not melt the fillets: they are pressed in warm oil until they break down and vanish into it.
